canonical_statement: For a consistent family of transition probabilities, transition from time s to time u factors through every intermediate time t: P(s,u)(x,A) is the integral over y of P(t,u)(y,A) against P(s,t)(x,dy). In the time-homogeneous discrete case this says that the (m+n)-step kernel is the composition of the m-step and n-step kernels.
domain_and_universes: A measurable state space E; a time parameter and transition kernels P(s,t) : Kernel E E for s <= t. The candidate pinned Lean encoding instead uses natural step counts and powers of one endokernel.
quantifiers: ordered times s <= t <= u, or natural step counts m and n in the homogeneous discrete specialization
hypotheses: each P(s,t) is a transition probability kernel with the measurability needed for kernel composition
the family is the transition family of the selected Markov model, or its composition consistency is derived from the selected construction
time homogeneity if the single-kernel power encoding is selected
conclusion: P(s,u)(x,A) = integral P(t,u)(y,A) dP(s,t)(x,dy); equivalently P(s,u) = P(t,u) composed with P(s,t).

alternate_encodings.relationship: kernel equality form of the general equation
setwise integral form of the homogeneous discrete-time specialization

alternate_encodings.target: continuous-time transition semigroup P(t+s) = P(t) composed with P(s)

excluded_degenerate_cases: Not yet frozen. The statement phase must explicitly treat zero elapsed time, m = 0 or n = 0, empty or degenerate state spaces, measurable-set requirements, null-set conventions, killed/sub-Markov kernels, and nonhomogeneous transition families.
